outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Enterprise software, led by Salesforce, Zscaler and NetApp
strongest.reason: the group extended its rally as sentiment continues to shift toward AI boosting rather than disrupting SaaS and security platforms, with Salesforce up sharply and cybersecurity peers holding recent gains

strongest.area: Chips, led by AMD, TSM and the broader AI-compute complex
strongest.reason: Piper Sandler initiated bullish coverage across Nvidia, Broadcom, Arm, AMD and Marvell, citing GPU capacity sold out through 2028 and a compute market it sees quintupling to $2.2 trillion by 2030; TSM's 53% August revenue jump added further confirmation

weakest.area: AI hardware & EDA, led by Synopsys's sharp reversal
weakest.reason: Synopsys gave back its recent rebound as the agentic-AI EDA debate reignited following last week's Kimi K3 headlines, even as Cadence held up better with a modest gain

weakest.area: Macro-sensitive assets — gold and the broad market indices
weakest.reason: gold fell as the dollar firmed and Fed rate-hike odds climbed to roughly 80-90% ahead of next week's FOMC meeting, while SPY and QQQ eased slightly as the Strait of Hormuz oil spike added a fresh layer of caution

outlook.nextStep: The Sept 15-16 FOMC decision is now the dominant catalyst, with hike odds near 80-90% after hot CPI and payrolls data — worth close attention given the direct line to yields, the dollar and risk appetite broadly. WTI's roughly 7% jump on the intensifying Strait of Hormuz conflict is the bigger wildcard and worth watching for follow-through into the Fed meeting; Synopsys's sharp reversal looks more like a name-specific re-rating of the EDA/AI story than a signal to extend to the broader software group, and is probably better watched than acted on yet.

signals.title: Oil surges to a six-week high as Strait of Hormuz conflict intensifies
signals.body: WTI jumped roughly 7% to just under $100 a barrel as US and Iranian forces continued strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, with tanker traffic through the chokepoint thinning further. The escalation comes just days ahead of the Fed's rate decision, raising the stakes for how oil-driven inflation pressure factors into the outlook.
signals.focus: the clearest macro risk heading into next week's Fed meeting; worth close monitoring for follow-through rather than reacting to any single session's move

signals.title: Fed rate-hike odds firm to roughly 80-90% ahead of Sept 15-16 FOMC
signals.body: Hotter-than-expected August core CPI and strong payrolls data have pushed markets' pricing of a 25bp hike at next week's meeting to around 80-90%, up from roughly 60-74% earlier in the month. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to nearly 4.98% as a result, even as oil's spike added a separate inflation crosscurrent.
signals.focus: the single most important catalyst of the week; probably better watched than traded ahead of Wednesday's decision and press conference

signals.title: Oracle extends rebound as cloud growth story regains favor
signals.body: Oracle rose another ~2.6% to around $161, recovering more of its post-earnings dip. The move suggests investors are giving more weight to the ~30% y/y cloud-infrastructure growth than to the debt load tied to its AI capex buildout, at least for now.
signals.focus: worth a closer look given the strong growth trajectory, though the capex/debt debate is probably better tracked over the next few quarters than reacted to on any single day's bounce

signals.title: Synopsys reverses sharply as EDA/agentic-AI debate reignites
signals.body: Synopsys fell about 6%, giving back its recent recovery, while Cadence held up with a modest gain. The split suggests the market hasn't settled on how big a threat AI-driven chip-design tools like Kimi K3 pose to incumbent EDA vendors.
signals.focus: worth watching closely for whether this is a one-day reversal or the start of a more lasting re-rating of the EDA group

signals.title: Intuitive Surgical jumps on UBS upgrade
signals.body: Intuitive Surgical rose roughly 5% after UBS upgraded the stock to Buy with a $500 price target, helping offset some of the recent valuation reset tied to JNJ's FDA-authorized Ottava soft-tissue robotic surgery platform.
signals.focus: a notable sentiment shift worth a closer look, though the underlying JNJ competitive overhang hasn't gone away

signals.title: Enterprise software and cybersecurity extend rally on eased AI-disruption fears
signals.body: Salesforce led gains along with Zscaler and NetApp, continuing a shift in sentiment toward AI as a tailwind rather than a threat for SaaS and security platforms. Adobe and Palantir also advanced, while ServiceNow held flat ahead of its Sept 16 Investor Day.
signals.watch: CRM, ADBE, PLTR, ZS, NTAP, CRWD
signals.focus: a continuing trend worth tracking, though the pace of recent gains may be due for some consolidation

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum extend gains as crypto sentiment turns greedy
signals.body: Bitcoin traded near $77,270 and Ethereum near $2,540, both higher, with the Crypto Fear & Greed Index around 63 (Greed). A Senate procedural vote on the revised 630-page CLARITY Act is scheduled for Sept 15, targeting decentralized-in-name-only protocols.
signals.focus: the Sept 15 regulatory vote is worth keeping an eye on given its potential to move sentiment in either direction
